questions.question: What happens when a muscle attached to a bone contracts?
options: It exerts a force on the bone, causing it to move.
It pushes the bone away from the joint.
It dissolves the joint fluid to allow easier sliding.
It temporarily weakens the bone structure.

questions.question: What is the name of the scientific field that studies the movement of the skeleton and muscles?
options: Biochemistry
Biomechanics
Bioengineering
Biophysics

questions.question: What term is used to describe the turning effect of a force when a bone pivots around a joint?
options: Moment
Friction
Acceleration
Tension

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the turning effect (moment) when a bone pivots at a joint?
options: Its size cannot be measured or calculated.
Its size is always the same regardless of the force applied.
Its size can be calculated using force and distance.
It is only present when a bone is completely still.

questions.question: What is the specific place where two or more bones meet in the human body called?
options: A ligament
A tendon
A joint
A marrow

questions.question: What is the main function of skeletal muscles in relation to bones?
options: Muscles can move bones.
Muscles produce calcium to strengthen bones.
Muscles convert bones into cartilage.
Muscles absorb impacts to keep bones soft.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how muscles exert force on bones?
options: Muscles can only push, by expanding.
Muscles can both pull and push equally.
Muscles can only pull, by contracting, and cannot push.
Muscles cannot pull or push; they only stabilize.

questions.question: Because muscles can only pull, how do they typically work to move a bone back and forth at a joint?
options: In antagonistic pairs, working together
As single muscles that can reverse their force
By relying on gravity to pull the bone back
In groups of four, all contracting at the same time

questions.question: What type of structures does the human body contain to allow movement and internal function?
options: Only rigid cartilage tubes
Muscles
Exoskeletal plates
Hydrolastic pumps

questions.question: What type of structure are muscles in the human body?
options: A type of tissue made up of specialised cells
Non-living protein fibres that do not contain cells
Homogeneous liquid structures without any cells
Mineralised structures similar to teeth

questions.question: Which two states can muscle tissue actively alternate between to function?
options: Dissolving and solidifying
Contracting and relaxing
Freezing and melting
Calcifying and softening

questions.question: Which of the following substances do muscles require in order to contract?
options: Carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Sugar and oxygen
Protein and salt water
Calcium and carbon monoxide

questions.question: What are the three main types of muscle that have different roles in the body's organ systems?
options: Rough muscle, smooth muscle, and bone muscle
Cardiac muscle, smooth muscle, and skeletal muscle
Soft muscle, hard muscle, and flexible muscle
Brain muscle, lung muscle, and stomach muscle

questions.question: What makes up the internal skeleton of the human body?
options: Cartilage plates only
A network of fluid-filled tubes
A skeleton made up of bones
Chitinous segments

questions.question: How is a joint defined in the human skeletal system?
options: The outer protective layer of any bone
A place where two or more bones meet
The soft center of a long bone
The point where a muscle attaches to a tendon

questions.question: What are two of the primary functions of the human skeleton?
options: Storing air and digesting food particles
Supporting the body and protecting organs and tissues
Pumping blood and contracting to generate body heat
Generating electrical signals and filtering waste

questions.question: Which statement is true about the nature of bones in a living human?
options: They are made of living tissue made up of cells.
They are entirely dead, mineralised structures with no cells.
They are made of solid protein fibers containing no water or cells.
They are hollow tubes filled only with air and no living cells.

questions.question: Where in the body are red and white blood cells produced?
options: In the bone marrow
In the skeletal muscles
In the joints between bones
In the outer layer of the skin
